Prevention: Use clean planting materials from inspected fields (RAB or
Remove weeds to discourage habitat for the vectors.
Uproot and bury volunteers plants in the fields
Crop rotation with cereals such as maize or leguminous crops (beans or soya bean)
Monitoring: Start observing symptoms immeditely after sprouting when young leaves are developed and continue twice a month
Observe leaves for symptoms twice a month.
Observe for green yellowish areas (mosaic), leaf deformation, reduction in size of young leaves and stunting of diseased plants in severe cases
Take action when one infected plant is observed
Direct Control: Uproot and bury infected plants when symptoms appear.
Restrictions: There is no chemical control against viruses
Use of pesticides to control vectors (whiteflies) on cassava is not pratical: insecticides can kill natural enemies such as
Apoanagyrus lopezi (released before 1990 to control cassava mealybugs) and
Typhlodromalus aripo (natural enemy of cassava green mites).
Protection equipments (PPE) and follow the instructions on the product label.
